conviction_note: Q3 revenue is close to pre-released: the company raised its guide twice in September, the second time on the last day of the quarter, and consensus sits on that guide floor. So the print turns on the Q4/2027 guide, the recurring royalty run-rate after Q3 catch-up royalties, and any new licences after the ITC institution. The stock round-tripped about 38% from its 1 Oct high to below its pre-licence level with no company news, which argues up, while the +8.7 vol-point put skew and the risk of a sequential Q4 decline argue down. That gives p_up 54, against the name's own large reaction scale (abs 14). The findings sum to +1.5 and the scaled number is +1.1; the two measurements agree in sign and roughly in size.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue of more than $186.4m: the company guide of more than 30% sequential growth on Q2's $143.35m, raised 2026-09-30 (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/VICR/vicor-corporation-raises-q3-2026-revenue-itqdkfftslv3.html). Consensus is $187.2m revenue / $1.39 EPS at Zacks (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/buy-sell-hold-vicor-stock-162800787.html, 2026-10-15) and $187.03m / $1.32 at MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-vicor-vicr-expected-to-post-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-10-13/). Revenue is sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing estimates. No sourced Q4 2026 consensus was found; the FY2026 guide of more than $600m from the Q2 call (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-vicor-co-stock/) is the only forward anchor.
positioning_check: Short interest is 3.3% of float with 1.4 days to cover (Equibles, snapshot 2026-08-19, https://equibles.com/stocks/VICR); Benzinga shows 7.0% of float (2026-08-28, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VICR/sentiment). No October figure was found. Not a crowded short. Baseline: 25-delta skew +8.71 vol points (downside paid), ATM IV 102%, put/call OI 1.02, 5-day run-up -21.7%, 20-day -9.3%, 46.5% below the 52-week high. The October drawdown ran on light volume: the 2026-10-15 session was about 80% below average volume at midday (MarketBeat). Insiders own about 28%.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue is essentially pre-announced. Vicor raised its Q3 sequential growth guide from 'nearly 10%' to '>20%' on 2026-09-21, then to '>30%' (more than $186.4m on Q2's $143.35m) on 2026-09-30, the last day of the quarter. Consensus revenue of $187.0-187.2m sits on that floor. Vicor's last two quarters beat consensus revenue by 2-4% (Q2 $143.35m vs $138.37m; Q1 $113.0m vs $110.8m), so a small beat over the floor is the likely print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat revenue ($143.35m vs $138.37m) and EPS ($1.04 vs $0.65), and the stock fell 7.05% on the licensing-timing caveat. Beats of the quarter alone have not paid on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. Consensus moved up 120% in 30 days to the guide floor (Zacks), and the guide was issued with the quarter already complete. Only the size of the excess over '>30%' is open, and Vicor's guide wording ('nearly', '>') has been conservative.
findings.independence: The consensus figures come from separate sources: Zacks $187.2m (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/buy-sell-hold-vicor-stock-162800787.html) and MarketBeat $187.03m (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-vicor-vicr-expected-to-post-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-10-13/). The guide itself is the company's single document.

findings.finding: The Q3 jump is royalty-driven and probably includes non-recurring catch-up. Both September raises were attributed to royalties from the new non-exclusive VPD licence, and the Sept 30 raise to 'increased royalties' was booked at quarter end. On the Q2 call management said the Q2 licence's $15m was a termination-clause recognition, falling to $5m in Q3 and $10m a quarter after. The FY2026 guide of more than $600m, against H1 $256.4m plus Q3 above $186.4m, implies Q4 of only about $157m or more. A sequentially lower Q4 guide is therefore a real possibility.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 royalty of $21.7m included a catch-up, and Q4 2025 royalty fell 33% to $14.5m. The Q3 2025 print (2025-10-21) still moved +30.33%, so a catch-up quarter has been bought before. The Q2 2026 print fell 7.05% on a forward-licensing caveat, so the forward line moves this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS has been revised to the Q3 guide, but no sourced Q4 consensus reflects how much of the Q3 royalty recurs. Vicor has not split the September royalty between one-time and run-rate. If the market had priced a Q4 step-down, previews would carry a Q4 figure below Q3, and none does.
findings.independence: The Q4 2025 royalty step-down after the Q3 2025 catch-up is from a different period and source (https://www.alphaspread.com/market-news/earnings/vicor-raises-q3-2026-revenue-growth-guidance-on-new-licensing-royalties, search summary). This is an inference from the company's own numbers, not a confirmed Q4 figure.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-09 the USITC instituted 337-TA-1526 on Vicor's VPD patent ('734) against Delta, Infineon, Luxshare, Monolithic Power Systems and others; Vicor's 12 Oct release adds Flex, Celestica, Quanta, Foxconn and Ingrasys. Vicor is seeking a limited exclusion order and cease-and-desist orders. The CEO said on Sept 21 that four OEMs/hyperscalers hold licences and that an early licence still comes 'with a low royalty rate'. The call is the first chance for management to quantify licensing after institution, or to name new licensees.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Licensing news has moved the stock: the 2026-09-16 licence +11-18%, the 2026-09-21 royalty raise +19.9%, the 2026-09-30 raise +6.8%. The Q2 call's 'licensing may wait for the 2027 final determination' caveat preceded a -7.05% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The institution is public, and the stock fell from $245 to $191.50 in the days after Vicor disclosed it (Oct 12), so no licensing upside is visible in the price. If it were priced, the stock would sit near its Oct 1 level rather than below its pre-licence Sep 17 level. The caveat is that management previously said new licences may wait for the 2027 final determination, so the upside is uncertain.
findings.independence: Focus Taiwan reports the respondents and Delta's response (https://focustaiwan.tw/business/202610110004, 2026-10-11). The four-licensee statement is in the Sept 21 release (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/VICR/vicor-corporation-raises-q3-2026-revenue-yk2virh0imov.html).

findings.finding: The price round-tripped below the level before both guidance raises with no company-specific negative. The stock went from about $216 on 2026-09-17 to $308.59 on 2026-10-01, then to $191.50 on 2026-10-16 (-38% from the peak), and sits at about $203 on Oct 19. Coverage attributes the fall to profit-taking and an AI-infrastructure/semis sell-off, on volume about 80% below average on Oct 15. Consensus PT is $391.67 and Zacks Rank is #1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 5 of the last 7 prints rose. The median absolute reaction is 16.55% and the maximum +30.33% (Q3 2025, a royalty catch-up quarter).
findings.why_not_priced: Spot is now below the price before the licence news and both raises, so the raised Q3 adds nothing to the price on a simple read. The option market disagrees (+8.7 vol-point put skew). The case that the skew is wrong is narrow: the drop came on sector beta and light volume, not on any company document. This is partly an unexplained drawdown, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Big Moves (2026-10-16) attributes the -12.9% day to the AI-spending sell-off (https://bigmoves.substack.com/p/big-moves-october-16-2026). MarketBeat (2026-10-15) found no company news and recorded low volume (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-vicor-nasdaq-vicr-shares-down-105-time-to-sell-2026-10-15/).

findings.finding: Product demand and capacity point to a ramp. One-year backlog rose 26% q/q to $379.7m in Q2 (+145% y/y) with book-to-bill above 1. Management guided Advanced Products to double-digit sequential growth in Q3 and said Fab-1 is 'approaching capacity utilization'. On 2026-09-11 Vicor bought sites for Fab-2/Fab-3 (nearly 1m sq ft) in New Hampshire, funded from $453.6m of cash. The Q3 backlog number and the capex plan land on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 backlog grew 26% and the stock still fell 7.05% on the licensing caveat, so backlog alone has not carried the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 backlog figure is not yet known and no preview estimates it. Expansion capex is funded from cash and corroborated by backlog, so it is a ramp signal and not a financing negative. The capacity ceiling may cap product upside this quarter, which is why the size is small.
findings.independence: The fab-site purchase release (https://manufacturingdigital.com/globenewswire/3360412, 2026-09-11) is a separate company document. The Q2 call transcript (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-vicor-co-stock/) gives the capacity-utilisation and second-fab comments.

findings.finding: The CEO keeps selling under a 10b5-1 plan: 20,000 shares at $316.13 on 2026-10-01, and about 320,700 shares (~$105.9m) over six months per Quiver. Insiders sold 27,053 shares worth $7.75m in the last 90 days, with no purchases.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not a print line. Sales have continued through both up and down prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the sales are planned and public in Form 4s. It remains a small overhang on the multiple.

outside_window.finding: The ITC 337-TA-1526 target date is to be set within 45 days of institution, and the investigation typically runs 12-16 months. The final determination in the second case, which management tied new licensing to, is due in 2027.

searched_and_found_nothing: A company-specific cause for the 2026-10-08 to 10-16 drawdown: no downgrade, filing or customer news found. MarketBeat and Quiver both say no news.
An October 2026 short-interest settlement: none found, latest is August.
A Q4 2026 or updated FY2026 revenue consensus: none sourced. Seeking Alpha's $547.6m FY figure is dated March 2026 and stale.
A Needham downgrade: the only 'downgraded by Needham' item found is from October 2023.
The licensee's identity or the September royalty dollar amount: undisclosed in both September releases.
Q2 10-Q notes on licence terms and customer concentration: the fetched text was truncated before the notes.

rejected_candidates.detail: The same four-licensee statement as the Sept 21 company release, already in the ITC/licensing finding.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly up, against the +8.7 vol-point put skew, though in line with a stock that has already fallen 21.7% in five days. The only negative of size, a royalty catch-up implying a lower Q4, agrees with the skew. That tension is why p_up sits at 54 and not higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (finding inside what the company guided): the Q3 pre-released revenue finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3.

Lessons 5 and 7 (an unexplained drawdown is not evidence; a sign against a strong skew needs a reason): the round-trip positioning finding cut from +2.5 to +1.0, kept because sector-selloff attribution and light volume give a partial explanation.
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the ITC/licensing finding cut from +1.5 to +1.0, because management itself said new licences may wait for the 2027 final determination.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage / understatement): abs_move_pct is held at 14 against the name's own median of 16.55, not shrunk further; only the pre-released quarter takes it below the median.
Lesson 3 (baseline tension): p_up moved from 55 to 54; expected_move_pct went from 1.3 to 1.12.
Lesson 4 (financing): the fab-site purchase and capex are funded from cash and corroborated by backlog, so they are not signed negative. No change from the draft.
